bill.title: A bill to authorize the Department of Justice to provide grant funding to accredited nonprofit organizations to provide better access to needed training for law enforcement officers in rural and smaller communities.
bill.latestActionText: Read twice and referred to the Committee on the Judiciary.

classification.plainSummary: This bill would authorize the Department of Justice to award grants to accredited nonprofit organizations. Those nonprofits would use the funding to provide training for law enforcement officers working in rural and smaller communities. The bill aims to improve access to training that these officers currently need but may lack.

industries.rationale: Nonprofit organizations focused on law enforcement training and public safety advocacy would be eligible grant recipients under this program.

method.formula: score = Σ_industries ( donorShare(industry) × billWeight(industry) ), where billWeight = classifierConfidence / Σ classifierConfidence. Range 0–1, read as a weighted share of disclosed itemized money.

disclaimer: This tool places two public records next to each other: who donated to a member of Congress, and what that member legislated on. Any overlap you see is a correlation, not causation. It is not evidence of a quid pro quo, of influence, or of wrongdoing. Legislators routinely receive support from industries in their district for the same reason they legislate on them: those industries are there.
